chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from Abdullah ibn Hammad Al-Ansari, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever visits the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), knowing his right, will be forgiven for what preceded of his sin and what followed.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (a.s.) with knowledge of his rights?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores that Ziyarah is not merely a physical act but a spiritual affirmation of Imam al-Husayn’s (a.s.) unique station and covenantal rights. The promise of comprehensive forgiveness—encompassing both past and future sins—highlights the transformative power of recognizing the Ahl al-Bayt’s authority, a concept deeply rooted in the doctrine of *Wilayah*. This reflects the Shia understanding that devotion to the Imams serves as a primary means of expiating sins and drawing closer to divine mercy.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Qāsim ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Ali narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ḥammād Al-Ansāri, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
Those who go to (the Ziyārah of) the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) knowing his rights will be forgiven for all of their past and future sins.
